cards.q: In C, what is 7 / 2 when both operands are int?
cards.a:
3

Integer division discards the fractional part; a floating operand would change the operation.

cards.q: C: int x=4; int y=x++; What are x and y afterwards?
cards.a:
x=5, y=4

Post-increment yields the old value and then increments x.

cards.q: C: int x=4; int y=++x; What are x and y afterwards?
cards.a:
x=5, y=5

Pre-increment increments first and yields the new value.

cards.q: C: char s[]="SEBI"; What is sizeof(s)?
cards.a:
5

The array contains four characters and a terminating null byte.

cards.q: C: int a[5]; What does sizeof(a)/sizeof(a[0]) give in the same scope?
cards.a:
5

The array total size divided by one element size is the element count. This fails after array-to-pointer parameter adjustment.

cards.q: Which C expression has undefined behaviour?
cards.a:
Reading a[5] from int a[5]

Valid indices are 0 through 4. Out-of-bounds access is undefined.

cards.q: What must a recursive function have to terminate on intended inputs?
cards.a:
A reachable base case and progress toward it

A base case is insufficient if recursive calls never move toward it.

cards.q: C++: int x=2; int& r=x; r=8; What is x?
cards.a:
8

r is an alias for x. Assigning through r updates x.

cards.q: What does encapsulation primarily support?
cards.a:
Controlling access to state through an interface

Encapsulation groups state and behaviour and controls how state is accessed.

cards.q: Two methods with the same name but different parameter lists demonstrate what?
cards.a:
Overloading

Overloading distinguishes callable signatures; overriding replaces inherited behaviour.

cards.q: Java: int[] a={1,2}; int[] b=a; b[0]=9; What is a[0]?
cards.a:
9

Both references point to the same array object. No copy was made.

cards.q: What does a Java finally block generally provide?
cards.a:
Cleanup executed when leaving the try/catch flow

Finally is for cleanup; abnormal VM termination is an exception to the usual execution rule.

cards.q: Python: a=[1,2]; b=a[:]; b.append(3); What is len(a)?
cards.a:
2

Slicing copies the outer list; appending to b does not append to a.

cards.q: Python: a=[[1]]; b=a[:]; b[0].append(2); What is a?
cards.a:
[[1, 2]]

A shallow copy shares the nested list, so mutating that nested object is visible through both.

cards.q: What is Python len(set([1,1,2,3,3]))?
cards.a:
3

A set contains only distinct values: 1, 2 and 3.

cards.q: Which structure naturally implements breadth-first traversal?
cards.a:
Queue

BFS processes discovered vertices in first-in-first-out order.

cards.q: Which structure is used for matching nested parentheses?
cards.a:
Stack

Each closing bracket must match the most recent unmatched opening bracket.

cards.q: Binary search requires what property of its search space?
cards.a:
An ordered or monotonic search condition

It discards half the space based on an order or monotonic predicate.

cards.q: What is the worst-case time of binary search on a sorted array?
cards.a:
O(log n)

The remaining interval is halved on each step.

cards.q: Inserting at the head of a singly linked list, given the head, takes what time?
cards.a:
O(1)

Only the new node link and the head pointer need updating.

cards.q: Which traversal of a BST with distinct keys gives ascending order?
cards.a:
Inorder

Left subtree, root, right subtree follows the BST ordering invariant.

cards.q: A min-heap guarantees which relationship?
cards.a:
Each parent is no greater than its children

The heap invariant is local parent-child order, not total sorted order.

cards.q: Building a binary heap bottom-up from n values takes what time?
cards.a:
O(n)

Most nodes are near leaves and require little work; the sum of sift-down costs is linear.

cards.q: A hash table has n entries and m buckets. Its load factor is?
cards.a:
n/m

Load factor measures entries relative to capacity or bucket count.

cards.q: Which sorting algorithm has O(n squared) worst case despite O(n log n) average behaviour?
cards.a:
Quicksort

Repeatedly highly unbalanced partitions make quicksort quadratic.

cards.q: A stable sort preserves what?
cards.a:
Relative order of equal-key items

Stability is useful when composing sorts on multiple keys.

cards.q: What property commonly makes dynamic programming useful?
cards.a:
Overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure

DP stores subproblem results and combines them according to a recurrence.

cards.q: For 0/1 knapsack, can an item be chosen repeatedly?
cards.a:
No

0/1 means each item is either selected once or not selected.

cards.q: With coins 1, 3, 4, how many coins optimally make 6?
cards.a:
2

3+3 uses two coins. Greedy 4+1+1 uses three and is not optimal here.

cards.q: How many overlapping occurrences of ABA are in ABABA?
cards.a:
2

Matches start at zero-based positions 0 and 2.

cards.q: What is the zero-based row-major offset of element [2][1] in a matrix with 4 columns?
cards.a:
9

Offset = row*columns + column = 2*4+1.

cards.q: Which is valid JSON?
cards.a:
{"ok":true,"n":null}

JSON needs quoted keys, lowercase literals and no trailing comma.

cards.q: Dijkstra’s standard correctness guarantee requires which edge-weight condition?
cards.a:
Non-negative weights

Negative edges can invalidate the greedy finalisation step.

cards.q: A topological ordering exists for which directed graphs?
cards.a:
Acyclic directed graphs

A directed cycle prevents an ordering with every edge going forward.

cards.q: Which key uniquely identifies a row and is selected as the principal identifier?
cards.a:
Primary key

A primary key is the chosen candidate key and disallows null values.

cards.q: Which relational operation selects rows satisfying a condition?
cards.a:
Selection

Selection filters rows; projection selects attributes.

cards.q: SQL: Which clause filters groups after aggregation?
cards.a:
HAVING

WHERE filters input rows, while HAVING filters grouped results.

cards.q: SQL: What does COUNT(column) exclude?
cards.a:
NULL values in that column

COUNT(column) counts non-null values; COUNT(*) counts rows.

cards.q: SQL: What predicate correctly tests a null value?
cards.a:
IS NULL

SQL uses three-valued logic; ordinary comparison with null is unknown.

cards.q: Which join retains every left-table row even when there is no right match?
cards.a:
LEFT JOIN

A left outer join supplies nulls for the missing right-side values.

cards.q: How does UNION differ from UNION ALL?
cards.a:
UNION eliminates duplicate result rows

UNION has distinct semantics. Ordering is not guaranteed without ORDER BY.

cards.q: A transaction should happen entirely or not at all. Which ACID property is this?
cards.a:
Atomicity

Atomicity prevents partial transaction effects from being committed.

cards.q: Which ACID property concerns persistence after commit?
cards.a:
Durability

Committed changes should survive the failures covered by the system guarantees.

cards.q: For BCNF, every nontrivial functional dependency X → Y must satisfy what?
cards.a:
X is a superkey

BCNF requires every determinant of a nontrivial dependency to be a superkey.

cards.q: Which index structure is especially suitable for ordered range scans?
cards.a:
B+ tree

Sorted leaf entries and leaf links allow efficient range traversal.

cards.q: What does a window aggregate usually preserve compared with GROUP BY?
cards.a:
Individual input rows

A window computes over related rows without necessarily collapsing them into grouped rows.

cards.q: Which OSI layer handles routing between networks?
cards.a:
Network

The network layer deals with logical addressing and routing.

cards.q: Which transport protocol provides ordered reliable byte-stream delivery?
cards.a:
TCP

TCP uses sequence numbers, acknowledgements and retransmissions.

cards.q: What service usually resolves hostnames to IP addresses?
cards.a:
DNS

DNS provides name resolution; DHCP supplies network configuration.

cards.q: How many total IPv4 addresses are in a /26 subnet?
cards.a:
64

There are 6 host bits, so 2^6 = 64 total addresses. Traditional usable-host count is 62.

cards.q: An Ethernet switch normally forwards frames using which address?
cards.a:
Destination MAC

Layer-2 switches use their learned MAC forwarding table.

cards.q: What is ARP used for in an IPv4 LAN?
cards.a:
Resolving a local IPv4 address to a link-layer address

ARP maps an on-link IPv4 destination or next hop to its MAC address.

cards.q: Which protocol is associated with sending email?
cards.a:
SMTP

SMTP transports outgoing mail. POP3 and IMAP are mainly for mailbox access.

cards.q: What does TCP flow control mainly protect?
cards.a:
The receiver from excessive incoming data

The receiver window limits how much unacknowledged data the receiver can accept.

cards.q: Which CIA property is harmed when unauthorised users read confidential records?
cards.a:
Confidentiality

Confidentiality controls disclosure to unauthorised parties.

cards.q: A record is altered without authorisation. Which CIA property is directly affected?
cards.a:
Integrity

Integrity concerns correctness and unauthorised modification.

cards.q: Which combination represents two distinct authentication factors?
cards.a:
Password and hardware security key

Knowledge plus possession is multifactor. Two knowledge secrets are the same factor type.

cards.q: Which control most directly prevents SQL injection in query parameters?
cards.a:
Parameterized queries

Bind values as data rather than concatenating them into executable SQL.

cards.q: Passwords should generally be stored using what?
cards.a:
A salted password hashing function

A deliberately costly password hash with a unique salt limits offline guessing and precomputed attacks.

cards.q: A digital signature is typically created with which key?
cards.a:
Signer’s private key

Verification uses the corresponding public key. Signing does not itself encrypt the message.

cards.q: Which policy best follows least privilege?
cards.a:
Grant only necessary access and review it

Limit access by role and task, and review it as needs change.

cards.q: What distinguishes an IPS from a purely passive IDS?
cards.a:
An IPS can actively block traffic

An intrusion prevention system can intervene; detection alone alerts.

cards.q: Python: list(range(1,6,2)) gives what?
cards.a:
[1, 3, 5]

range excludes the stop value and advances by the supplied step.

cards.q: In pandas, which selector is primarily position-based?
cards.a:
iloc

iloc selects by integer positions; loc uses labels or boolean masks.

cards.q: A join key appears 3 times on the left and 2 times on the right. How many matching rows can an inner join produce for it?
cards.a:
6

Every left match combines with every right match: 3*2 rows.

10

R uses one-based vector indexing.

cards.q: R: mean(c(2,NA,6), na.rm=TRUE) gives what?
cards.a:
4

Removing the missing observation leaves (2+6)/2 = 4.

cards.q: Which ETL stage standardises inconsistent date formats?
cards.a:
Transform

Transformation cleans and maps source values into the target representation.

cards.q: Moving from daily totals to monthly totals is which OLAP operation?
cards.a:
Roll-up

Roll-up aggregates to a coarser level of a hierarchy.

cards.q: What should a fact table’s grain define?
cards.a:
What one row represents

A clear grain prevents mixing measures at incompatible levels of detail.

cards.q: Which regex matches exactly three ASCII digits and nothing else?
cards.a:
^[0-9]{3}$

Anchors require the whole string and {3} sets the exact repetition count.

cards.q: In a shell script, what does $# represent?
cards.a:
Number of positional arguments

The argument count is separate from $1 (first argument) and $? (previous status).

cards.q: Which shell exit status conventionally indicates success?
cards.a:
0

Zero means success by convention; nonzero usually signals failure.

cards.q: What does a shell pipe connect?
cards.a:
Left command stdout to right command stdin

A pipe streams one program’s standard output to another’s standard input.

cards.q: Why quote "$name" in a shell command?
cards.a:
To preserve it as one argument despite spaces

Double quotes allow variable expansion while preventing word splitting and pathname expansion of the result.

cards.q: Why commonly run sort before uniq?
cards.a:
uniq combines adjacent duplicate lines

Identical lines must be adjacent to be consolidated by uniq.

cards.q: What is a primary market transaction?
cards.a:
An issuer selling newly issued securities

The primary market raises funds through new issuance; secondary trading transfers existing securities.

cards.q: What does diversification mainly reduce?
cards.a:
Asset-specific risk

Combining imperfectly correlated exposures can reduce concentration risk, but does not guarantee returns.

cards.q: An equity share generally represents what?
cards.a:
An ownership interest

Equity is a residual ownership claim with uncertain returns.

cards.q: What is a depository’s core role?
cards.a:
Holding securities electronically and facilitating transfers

Electronic holdings and book-entry transfers are central depository functions.

cards.q: Which instrument gives its holder a right, without an obligation, to buy at a specified strike under its terms?
cards.a:
Call option

A call provides the purchase right; a put provides the sale right.

cards.q: What does a mutual fund NAV represent?
cards.a:
Net assets per unit

NAV divides the fund’s net asset value by its outstanding units.

cards.q: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
cards.a:
Each of the applicants is ready.

Each is the singular subject; the phrase of the applicants does not change agreement.

cards.q: Choose the correct usage.
cards.a:
The results affect the decision.

Affect is the verb meaning influence; results is plural and takes affect.

cards.q: Which word is closest in meaning to mitigate?
cards.a:
Reduce the severity of

Mitigate means make less severe; it does not mean eliminate.

cards.q: Which sentence uses parallel structure?
cards.a:
The role requires analysing data, writing reports and reviewing controls.

All three coordinated activities use the same grammatical form.

cards.q: All A are B. Some B are C. Does some A are C necessarily follow?
cards.a:
No

The B-C overlap may be entirely outside A.

cards.q: A > B and B >= C. What follows?
cards.a:
A > C

Combining a strict greater-than with a non-strict greater-than gives a strict greater-than.

cards.q: A candidate ranks 7th from the top and 14th from the bottom. How many candidates are there?
cards.a:
20

Add the two ranks and subtract one to avoid counting the candidate twice.

cards.q: A person walks 6 km east then 8 km north. What is displacement magnitude?
cards.a:
10 km

The straight-line displacement follows the Pythagorean theorem: sqrt(36+64).

cards.q: A value rises 20% then falls 20%. Relative to the original, it is now?
cards.a:
4% lower

Multipliers 1.2*0.8 = 0.96. The percentage changes have different bases.

cards.q: A does a job in 10 days and B in 15 days. Together they need?
cards.a:
6 days

Combined daily work rate is 1/10+1/15 = 1/6.

cards.q: A bag has 3 red and 2 blue balls. One is drawn uniformly. P(blue) is?
cards.a:
2/5

Two of the five equally likely outcomes are blue.

cards.q: How many ways can 2 people be selected from 5, ignoring order?
cards.a:
10

5 choose 2 = 5*4/2 = 10. Divide by two because each pair can be ordered in two ways.

cards.q: A train covers 150 km in 2.5 hours. Average speed is?
cards.a:
60 km/h

Average speed = total distance divided by total time.
